title: Possible stroke
summary: Use FAST, call emergency services immediately, and record onset or last-known-well time.
sources: 2024 American Heart Association and American Red Cross Guidelines for First Aid — Recognition of Stroke
actions: Use FAST: ask the person to smile, raise both arms, and repeat a simple sentence. Look for facial droop, arm drift, or abnormal speech.
Call emergency services immediately for any sign and say “possible stroke.” Record the exact symptom onset or last-known-well time.
Keep the person in a safe comfortable position and monitor breathing and alertness.
If unresponsive but breathing normally, use the recovery position. Start CPR if breathing becomes absent or abnormal.
Do not cancel the call if symptoms resolve; a transient ischemic attack is also urgent.
prohibitions: Do not give aspirin because bleeding cannot be excluded outside hospital.
Do not give food, drink, or oral medicine because swallowing may be unsafe.
Do not wait for improvement or let the person drive.

emergencyCall.text: Any new face droop, one-sided weakness, or speech change is an emergency even if it resolves.
